terms.meaning: The program in which a language model chooses ideas and code checks every number.
Plain code, no AI: it tries every combination of settings and builds the best clues for each.
The broadcaster's forecast: the runs per over so far, times 20.
Always guess the typical final total, whatever the score at 10 overs.
One try: a set of clues together with settings.
The facts about an innings a model may use, such as wickets at 10 overs.
Choices made before learning starts, such as how many seasons to learn from.
Seasons used again and again to choose between ideas.
The one season kept sealed until the end, then scored once.

terms.technical: the model chosen on the check seasons
terms.meaning: The idea that scored best on the check seasons.

definitions.brute_force: The brute-force search is plain code, no AI: it tries every combination of settings and, inside each, adds clues one at a time, keeping whichever cuts the miss most. It is the yardstick: if the agent can't match it, its reasoning isn't adding anything.
definitions.brute_force_technical: Technically it is a grid search over 24 combinations of three hyperparameters (which innings, how many seasons, how much recent seasons count), with greedy forward selection of features in each cell.
definitions.brute_force_honest: "Brute-force" refers to the settings only: it does not try every possible set of clues (2^19, about 524,000).
